learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts on the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application for solving engineering problems.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Critically and constructively evaluate the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem.
Solve complex problems, autonomously, in the field of the discipline.
Extract conclusions from practical or experimental work and research carried out autonomously.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics: Position vector, velocity, acceleration. Rectilinear motion: uniform and uniformly accelerated. Circular motion: uniform and uniformly accelerated. Parabolic motion (2 dimensions).

Dynamics of a point and systems of points: Forces. Newton's Laws. Examples of forces: gravity, weight force; friction; elastic deformation forces. Particle systems. Centers of mass. Equations of dynamics of a particle system. Conservation of momentum.

Work and energy: Definition of work. Kinetic energy. Relationship between net work and change in kinetic energy. Potential energy. Calculation of potential energy: gravitational and elastic potential energy. Conservation of mechanical energy. Energy of a particle system.
Oscillations: Simple harmonic motion, kinematics and dynamics. Simple pendulum. Physical pendulum. Damped oscillations. Forced oscillations, resonance.
Mechanical waves: Wave motion. Harmonic waves. Interference. Some properties of waves. Sound: Doppler effect, sound waves and decibels.

Electrostatics and capacitors: Electric charge. Coulomb's Law. Electric field. Electric potential. Electrostatic energy. Concept of capacitance. Types of capacitors. Dielectrics. Capacitor association. Energy stored by a capacitor.

Electrokinetics: Current intensity. Ohm's Law. Electrical resistance. Resistor association. Joule's Law. Generators and receivers. DC circuits. Generalized Ohm's Law. Kirchhoff's Laws. Node and mesh methods. Charging and discharging of capacitors.
Alternating current: Sinusoidal alternating current. AC in passive elements. Concept of impedance. Generalized Ohm's Law for AC. Active, apparent and reactive power in AC.
Thermodynamics: Thermodynamic systems. Thermodynamic properties. Thermodynamic processes. The first principle in closed systems, cycles and open systems. The second principle.
Optics: Properties of light. Optical images. Interference and diffraction.
teaching_methods: Lectures (participatory, conferences, company visits, fair attendance)
Participatory classes (case resolution, role-playing, exercises, oral and written presentations, debates)
Integrated project work (including planning, design, execution, teamwork, use of Octave)
Classroom theory sessions (using multimedia and online platforms)
assessment_rules: To average with other parts, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 must be obtained in the type B written test of each semester. The final passing condition requires a final grade of 5 or higher and a minimum of 4 in the type B written tests. If these conditions are not met, the course is failed; the final grade will be 'Not Presented' if absent from the exam, or the exam grade with a maximum of 4 if present. In the second call, only type B written tests and the integrated project will be considered, primarily for students who could not attend continuous assessment for justified reasons.
